reason: Wording checked against the text of Anthony Bower's translation itself (the Anarchist Library PDF of the Bower edition with Herbert Read's foreword, extracted with pdftotext): Part One, The Rebel, ends: In our daily trials rebellion plays the same role as does the cogito in the realm of thought: it is the first piece of evidence. But this evidence lures the individual from his solitude. It founds its first value on the whole human race. I rebel—therefore we exist. The dash is U+2014 in Bower, exactly as proposed, and the sentence is the last of Part One before the heading Part Two: Metaphysical Rebellion, so the locator is right. Wikiquote files the line under Part Five, which is where Bower reprints it with a comma (I rebel, therefore we exist, said the slave); the Part One form with the dash is the one proposed, so the verifier's locator is the better one. Bower is the only published English translator of The Rebel; his translation appeared in 1953 (Hamish Hamilton) and, revised and complete, in 1954 and 1956 (Knopf, Vintage), and this sentence is the same in all of them. shipped.js: not shipped, no near line, Camus at 1 of 3 for the year (January only), not banned, no other Camus in February.
